Southwark DiocesanMulti-Trust Academy
St Stephen’s C of E Primary School
Welcome to St Stephen's Church of England Primary School – a place where every child is truly known and valued, and where every family becomes part of our school family.
As a one-form entry school in the heart of Lewisham, we are proud of the warm relationships that make St Stephen's such a special place. We believe children thrive when they feel safe, happy and truly belong, and our dedicated staff work closely with families to ensure every child is supported, encouraged and celebrated as an individual.
Rooted in our Christian vision, we nurture children to become confident, positive and compassionate young people who are empowered to face life's challenges, embrace new opportunities and make a positive difference in the world. Our core values of kindness, honesty, self-control, respect and perseverance are woven through every aspect of school life, shaping not only what our children learn, but who they become.
St Stephen's is more than a school – it is a family. We would be delighted to welcome you and share what makes our community such a special place for children to learn, grow and flourish.

Values & Vision
Our School Vision Statement
Every member of our school family can stand as spiritual, confident, positive individuals, rooted in Christian values, empowered to face life’s challenges, reach their full potential and serve their community.
St Stephen’s 5 Core Values
As a Church of England School, our values are based on the Fruit of the Spirit; love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. (Galatians 5v 22-23)
Please have a look at our Values Brochure below. Our children are encouraged to use these values throughout the school day.
We also have 5 key Bible Verses, which the children learn and reflect on in collective worship and class. Have a look at our "5 For Life" below.
Our Spirituality Statement explains how St Stephen's approach to spiritual development is embodied by, and lived out through, the school's theologically rooted Christian vision.

Religious Education
Religious Education Vision Statement
Intent
At St Stephen's C of E Primary School, we believe Religious Education helps every child develop religious literacy, spirituality and respect for others. As a Church of England school serving a diverse community, we provide an inclusive environment where pupils learn about Christianity and a range of other faiths and worldviews. Through Religious Education, children explore questions of meaning, purpose and belief, reflect on their own experiences and values, and develop into thoughtful, compassionate and open-minded individuals who are prepared to contribute positively to a diverse and changing world.
Using the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education Agreed Syllabus, our carefully sequenced curriculum develops pupils' knowledge and understanding through the lenses of Believing, Thinking and Living. Pupils study Christianity as a living global faith while developing knowledge and appreciation of other religions and non-religious worldviews. Through enquiry, discussion and reflection, they learn to engage thoughtfully with different perspectives and understand how beliefs influence individuals, communities and society.
Implementation
Curriculum Progression
Religious Education is taught in accordance with the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education Agreed Syllabus. Two-thirds of the curriculum focuses on Christianity, with the remaining third exploring Islam, Judaism, Buddhism, Hinduism, Sikhism and non-religious worldviews.
Learning is structured around carefully sequenced Big Questions that encourage enquiry, discussion and reflection. From the Early Years to Year 6, pupils progressively develop their understanding of beliefs, practices, values and worldviews while exploring themes such as belonging, identity, justice and the meaning of a good life.
Knowledge and understanding build progressively through the three curriculum lenses, enabling pupils to make meaningful connections between faith, belief and everyday life. Religious Education is taught to all pupils, including those in the Early Years Foundation Stage, where learning is linked to the EYFS Early Learning Goals.
Teaching, learning and assessment are centred on the three lenses of the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education Agreed Syllabus:
• Believing (Theology) – exploring religious and non-religious beliefs, teachings and sources of authority
• Thinking (Philosophy) – questioning, reflecting on and evaluating beliefs, values and ideas
• Living (Human and Social Sciences) – examining how beliefs shape individuals, communities and the wider world
These lenses enable pupils to deepen their understanding, think critically and appreciate the diversity of beliefs within modern society.
Impact
By the end of Year 6, pupils leave St Stephen's as knowledgeable, reflective and respectful learners who understand Christianity as a diverse, living global faith and appreciate the beliefs and practices of other religions and worldviews. They are equipped to engage thoughtfully with different perspectives and contribute positively to life in a diverse society.
• Develop religious literacy through a secure understanding of Christianity, other world faiths and non-religious worldviews
• Understand Christianity as a diverse, living global faith
• Explore how beliefs, values and practices influence individuals and communities
• Demonstrate respect, empathy and understanding towards people of all faiths and none
• Reflect on spiritual, moral and philosophical questions about life, meaning and belief
• Understand the contribution of religion and belief to morality, relationships and society
• Make thoughtful connections between beliefs, values and ways of living
Assessment is ongoing through discussion, written and creative responses, enquiry-based activities and teacher assessment. Clear progression from Reception to Year 6 ensures every child develops secure knowledge, understanding and reflective thinking, enabling them to engage confidently with religious and non-religious worldviews.

Music
Music Curriculum Vision Statement
Intent
At St Stephen's C of E Primary School, we believe music is a powerful form of communication that inspires creativity, nurtures self-expression and celebrates the diversity of our world. Through our music curriculum, pupils develop confidence, musical knowledge and performance skills while gaining an appreciation of a wide range of musical traditions. We aim for every child to become a curious, expressive and reflective musician who enjoys creating, performing and listening to music, recognising music as a lifelong source of enjoyment, connection and cultural understanding.
We follow the Kapow Primary Music scheme, providing a carefully sequenced curriculum that meets the requirements of the National Curriculum and builds musical knowledge, skills and vocabulary progressively from EYFS to Year 6. Pupils develop as performers, composers, listeners and musicians through singing, composing, improvising, listening and performing. By revisiting and extending key musical concepts each year, children develop technical proficiency, creativity and confidence while learning to communicate ideas and emotions through music.
Implementation
Curriculum Progression
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that pupils build progressively on their musical knowledge and skills throughout their time at St Stephen's.
Learning is organised around five key strands that are revisited and developed each year:
• Listening and evaluating
• Improvising and composing
Children learn through practical, active music-making by listening, singing, playing instruments, composing, improvising and performing. Lessons encourage collaboration, creativity and reflection while developing technical skills alongside a deeper understanding of music. Pupils use increasingly sophisticated musical vocabulary to describe, analyse and evaluate their work.
Pupils revisit and deepen their understanding through a broad range of musical experiences, including:
• Instrumental performance
• Songs from different cultures and traditions
• Western classical music
The curriculum introduces children to music from a wide variety of historical periods, cultures, composers and musical traditions, helping them understand music as a universal language. Each unit builds on previous learning, ensuring clear progression in both musical knowledge and practical skills.
Learning is centred on developing pupils as confident musicians through:
• Listening and appraising
• Singing and performing
• Composing and improvising
• Understanding notation
• Developing musical vocabulary
Children learn to perform with increasing confidence, compose creatively, listen critically and respond thoughtfully to a wide range of musical styles.
Cross-Curricular Links
Music enriches learning across the wider curriculum through meaningful links with English, mathematics, history, geography, computing and PSHE. Pupils develop communication skills through singing and performance, mathematical understanding through rhythm and pattern, cultural awareness through music from different times and places, and digital skills through music technology. Music also supports pupils' personal development by fostering confidence, resilience, teamwork and self-expression.
Impact
By the end of Year 6, pupils leave St Stephen's as confident, creative and reflective musicians who enjoy performing, composing, improvising and listening with understanding. They have developed the knowledge, skills and musical vocabulary needed to appreciate diverse musical traditions and continue their musical journey beyond primary school.
• Perform confidently using their voices and a range of instruments
• Compose and improvise using increasingly sophisticated musical techniques
• Listen to and evaluate music from a wide range of genres, cultures and historical periods
• Use musical vocabulary accurately to describe and discuss music
• Demonstrate creativity, resilience and collaboration through shared musical experiences
• Develop a lifelong appreciation of music as a means of expression, enjoyment and cultural understanding
Assessment is ongoing through teacher observation, practical performances, compositions, pupil discussion and reflective evaluation. Clear progression from Reception to Year 6 ensures every child develops secure musical knowledge, practical skills and confidence before moving on to increasingly ambitious musical experiences.

Science
Science Curriculum Vision Statement
Intent
At St Stephen's C of E Primary School, we believe Science helps children make sense of the amazing world around them. We aim for every child to become curious, confident and thoughtful, asking questions, exploring ideas and learning from what they discover. Our curriculum inspires pupils to be rooted in an appreciation of God's creation and a secure understanding of the natural world, empowered with the scientific knowledge, enquiry skills and critical thinking needed to investigate, question and solve problems, and ready to serve by using science responsibly to care for others, protect the environment and make informed choices that positively impact their community and the wider world.
We follow the Kapow Primary Science scheme, which provides a carefully sequenced curriculum that meets the requirements of the National Curriculum and ensures knowledge, scientific enquiry skills and vocabulary build progressively from EYFS to Year 6.
Pupils develop their understanding across the key areas of biology, chemistry and physics while learning to work scientifically. Through practical investigations and enquiry-based learning, children ask questions, make observations, gather evidence, test ideas and draw conclusions, developing the curiosity and confidence to think like scientists.
Implementation
Curriculum Progression
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that pupils progressively develop both substantive scientific knowledge and disciplinary knowledge through scientific enquiry.
In Key Stage 1, children explore the world around them through observation, simple investigations and practical experiences while developing key scientific vocabulary. In Lower Key Stage 2, pupils deepen their understanding of topics including plants, animals, rocks, light, forces and electricity, carrying out increasingly structured enquiries. By Upper Key Stage 2, children investigate more complex concepts such as Earth and Space, evolution, inheritance and the human body, planning investigations, analysing results and explaining their thinking using accurate scientific language.
Throughout the curriculum, key concepts are revisited through a spiral approach, enabling pupils to strengthen prior learning, make meaningful connections and deepen their understanding over time.
Working Scientifically
Scientific enquiry is at the heart of our curriculum. Pupils develop the skills to:
• Ask scientific questions
• Make careful observations and measurements
• Plan and carry out investigations
• Record data using a range of methods
• Analyse, interpret and present findings
• Draw conclusions using evidence
These skills become increasingly sophisticated as pupils progress through the school, enabling them to think critically and work confidently as young scientists.
Our ambitious curriculum provides full coverage of the National Curriculum and is designed to be accessible for all learners. Knowledge and enquiry skills are carefully sequenced, allowing pupils to revisit and build upon prior learning while developing a secure understanding of scientific concepts. Inclusive teaching strategies ensure every child is supported and challenged to achieve their potential.
Cross-Curricular Links
Science enriches learning across the wider curriculum through meaningful links with mathematics, computing, Design and Technology, geography and PSHE. Pupils apply mathematical skills when measuring, recording and analysing data, use computing to present findings, and deepen their understanding of the natural world through wider curriculum topics. These connections help children develop transferable knowledge and skills across subjects.
Impact
By the end of Year 6, pupils leave St Stephen's as curious, knowledgeable and confident young scientists with a secure understanding of the scientific concepts and enquiry skills developed throughout their primary education. They are well prepared for the challenges of secondary science and equipped to think critically about the world around them.
• Demonstrate secure knowledge across biology, chemistry and physics
• Use scientific vocabulary accurately and confidently
• Ask thoughtful questions and plan fair scientific enquiries
• Make careful observations, record data accurately and interpret results
• Draw evidence-based conclusions and explain their thinking clearly
• Recognise the importance of science in understanding and caring for the world around them
Assessment is ongoing through practical investigations, retrieval practice, teacher questioning, pupil discussion and formative assessment. Clear progression from Reception to Year 6 ensures every child develops secure scientific knowledge, enquiry skills and critical thinking before moving on to increasingly challenging scientific learning.

SEND
An Inclusive Environment
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do at St. Stephen’s Primary School. We are proud of our strong Christian ethos, where every pupil is valued and fully included in all aspects of school life. We recognise that some pupils may require additional support or targeted interventions at different stages of their education, while others may need ongoing provision. School staff and leaders work together to ensure pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) are identified early and supported through high-quality teaching and additional interventions. This support is outlined in our SEND Information Report.
Our SEND provision is overseen by the Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo) Laura Scallon. For any queries regarding SEND at St. Stephen’s, please email admin@ststephensce.lewisham.sch.uk
Please click on the Lewisham Local Offer for support and information that is offered in the Lewisham Community.
Our Values and Vision Statement
Vision Statement
Every member of our school family can stand as spiritual, confident, positive individuals, rooted in Christian values, empowered to face life's challenges, reach their full potential and serve their community.
Intent
The Governing Body and staff at St. Stephen’s recognise and value the unique contribution of every pupil. We celebrate diversity in culture, faith and learning styles, and are committed to delivering an inclusive curriculum that enables all pupils to achieve their full potential, regardless of their needs or abilities.
We strive to raise achievement, remove barriers to learning, and improve access to both the curriculum and the physical environment. Pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) are respected, supported and treated as equal members of our school community.
To ensure early identification of SEND and timely, effective provision.
To create a culture and deploy resources that meet the needs of all pupils with SEND.
To enable pupils with SEND to achieve their full potential.
To adopt a pupil-centred approach to identifying, assessing and reviewing needs.
To provide full access to a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum, including the Early Years Foundation Stage and National Curriculum.
To work in partnership with parents and carers.
To take into account the views and aspirations of each pupil.
To collaborate with the Local Authority and external agencies through a multi-agency approach.
To ensure staff receive appropriate training and ongoing professional development.
To maintain high-quality teaching and effective provision for all pupils.
Implementation
At St. Stephen’s CE Primary School, every teacher and teaching assistant shares responsibility for supporting pupils with SEND. Our aim is for all pupils to enjoy school and develop academically, physically, socially and spiritually into well-rounded individuals.
Teachers deliver a creative, engaging and differentiated curriculum.
High expectations are maintained for all pupils.
Pupils are included in all aspects of school life wherever possible.
All pupils receive quality-first teaching, tailored to meet a range of needs.
Targeted group and individual interventions are provided where necessary, including support in:
Physical development
Social and emotional development
Our approach is holistic and may include specialist provision such as sports activities, regulation support, play therapy and Forest School sessions.
We actively promote strong parental involvement and offer workshops led by both internal staff and external specialists.
We work closely with a range of external professionals, including:
Educational Psychologists
Drumbeat Autism Outreach Team
Inclusion Outreach Services
Specific Learning Difficulties (SpLD) Team
Additional support includes:
A Speech and Language Therapist working in school weekly (half-termly blocks).
A Play Therapist providing weekly sessions for identified pupils.
Impact
The SENCo oversees all SEND provision and monitors its effectiveness. Evaluation is carried out through:
Individual Provision Maps (IEPs): Used to set personalised targets and track progress.
Data analysis: Pupils are assessed termly, with progress closely monitored to identify any underachievement.
Ongoing review: Ensuring interventions are effective and appropriately targeted.
Pupils with SEND make strong progress from their starting points.
Pupils develop independence and essential life skills.
Behaviour across the school remains consistently high.
Lewisham Local Offer
The Lewisham Local Offer provides clear, up-to-date information on services and support available for children and young people aged 0–25 with SEND, across education, health and social care.
Click here for more information.
Access to Medical Support
We ensure that pupils with medical needs are supported through well-established systems:
Regular liaison between the School Nurse and Inclusion Manager.
A clear policy for supporting pupils with medical conditions.
Staff trained in Paediatric First Aid.
Individual healthcare plans are followed for pupils with specific medical needs.
All staff trained in the use of EpiPens.
Clear procedures for administering medication in school.
Accurate record-keeping of all medical support provided.
SENDIASS
The Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Information Advice and Support Services (SENDIASS) offer information, advice and support for parents and carers of children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). This service is also offered directly to young people.
Lewisham special educational needs and disabilities information advice and support service (SENDIASS) offers independent information, advice and support.
You can access this service if you live in the borough and:
you care for a child or young person with SEND (up to 25 years old)
you are a young person with SEND aged 16 to 25

Fun at Forest School!
St Stephen's pupils have had a blast at Forest School this term!
🌿 Our Forest School sessions this term were full of creativity, exploration and fun! 🍃
🍂 In this session, using leaves, twigs, grasses and other natural treasures they found, the children designed and made beautiful leaf crowns 👑 before enjoying a range of other hands-on Forest School activities. 🌳 They worked together 🤝, used their imaginations 💡 and discovered more about the natural world around them 🐞, all while building confidence 💚 and enjoying the great outdoors. 🌞 It was a wonderful afternoon of learning through play! 🌼

Dining Room Etiquette
Our Dining Room Etiquette Competition entries were amazing!
Over the past few weeks, we have been running a Dining Room Etiquette Competition across the school to encourage children to think about the importance of good table manners and how they can help create a calm, respectful and enjoyable dining environment. Children were asked to produce a creative piece of work promoting positive dining habits. The response was incredible! We received a fantastic range of entries (some examples can be seen on the right), including songs, raps, poems and colourful posters. The standard was exceptionally high, making it extremely difficult to choose the winners. After much deliberation, we selected two winners from each class. Last week, these children proudly shared their entries in assembly, inspiring the rest of the school to continue demonstrating excellent dining room etiquette. As a result of the competition and the children's commitment to putting these good habits into practice, we have already noticed a significant improvement in our dining room. The atmosphere is calmer, children are speaking more quietly, showing excellent manners, and moving around the dining hall safely. It has made lunchtime a much more enjoyable experience for everyone. To recognise their fantastic efforts, all of our winners were invited to enjoy a special hot chocolate and muffin treat. It was a thoroughly deserved reward, and a wonderful opportunity to celebrate their creativity and positive contribution to school life. A huge well done to every child who took part. We are incredibly proud of the enthusiasm, imagination and maturity they showed throughout the competition, and we are confident these excellent dining habits will continue both in school and at home.

Art
Art Curriculum Vision Statement
Intent
At St Stephen's C of E Primary School, we believe every child should become a confident artist, imaginative creator, thoughtful critic and reflective learner with a love of art. Through our Art and Design curriculum, pupils develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to express themselves creatively, explore ideas and appreciate art from a wide range of cultures, traditions and historical periods.
We follow the Kapow Primary Art and Design scheme, providing a carefully sequenced curriculum that meets the requirements of the National Curriculum and builds knowledge and skills progressively from EYFS to Year 6.
Our curriculum develops pupils' understanding across five key strands:
• Making skills and formal elements
• Knowledge of artists
• Evaluating and analysing artwork
Pupils explore drawing, painting, sculpture, craft, textiles, printing, digital art and mixed media while developing creativity, resilience and an appreciation of artists from diverse cultures and artistic traditions.
Implementation
Curriculum Progression
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that pupils revisit the key disciplines of drawing, painting, sculpture, craft and design throughout their time at St Stephen's. Each unit builds on prior learning through a spiral curriculum, enabling children to deepen their understanding, refine technical skills and become increasingly independent artists.
In the Early Years, children explore materials, make marks and develop fine motor control through play and continuous provision. In Key Stage 1, pupils develop confidence with colour, line, shape, form and texture while learning about influential artists and experimenting with a range of media. By Key Stage 2, children undertake increasingly ambitious projects involving printing, textiles, digital art, photography, mixed media, installations and sculpture, applying their knowledge creatively while refining and evaluating their work.
Across all year groups, pupils study significant artists, designers and craft makers from different cultures and historical periods. These carefully selected studies broaden cultural
understanding and inspire children to develop their own artistic style and creative voice.
Learning is centred on creativity, technical skill and critical thinking. Pupils generate ideas, experiment with materials and techniques, use sketchbooks to develop and refine their thinking, and evaluate both their own work and the work of others using increasingly sophisticated artistic vocabulary.
Cross-Curricular Links
Art enriches learning across the wider curriculum through meaningful links with history, geography, English, science and RE. Many projects connect creatively to class topics, while opportunities to visit galleries and experience artwork first-hand help pupils develop a deeper appreciation of art and culture.
Impact
By the end of Year 6, pupils leave St Stephen's as confident, creative and reflective artists who have developed the knowledge, skills and confidence to continue their artistic journey at secondary school and beyond.
• Use a wide range of artistic techniques and media with confidence
• Develop and communicate original creative ideas
• Evaluate and refine their own work while responding thoughtfully to the work of others
• Understand and appreciate the work of significant artists, designers and craft makers
• Value art from a diverse range of cultures, traditions and historical periods
Assessment is ongoing throughout each unit through sketchbooks, practical outcomes, pupil discussion and teacher assessment. Clear progression from Reception to Year 6 ensures every child develops secure artistic knowledge, technical skills and creative confidence before moving on to increasingly ambitious artistic experiences.
